source.title: How much do language models memorize?
source.authors: J. X. Morris; Chawin Sitawarin; Chuan Guo; Narine Kokhlikyan; G. Suh; Alexander M. Rush; Kamalika Chaudhuri; Saeed Mahloujifar

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study measures test loss while varying training-set size and relates the resulting double-descent pattern to estimated model capacity. This is a conceptual test of the data-size claim using its own compression-based capacity measure.
record.gate_note: The study explicitly reports double descent in evaluation loss as training-set size varies. Figures 3 and 4 show separate model-size curves, but values are available only in the figures. Other reported findings about memorization, extraction, and membership inference do not measure test-error double descent and are not rows here.
record.test_reason: The study trains GPT-style Transformers of four sizes (1.7M–19.2M parameters) on FineWeb across training-set sizes and reports test loss. It plots test loss against a dataset-to-capacity ratio, where capacity is its own bits-per-parameter estimate, and claims double descent starts where data exceeds model capacity. That bears on the sample-wise version (V3) and the effective-complexity account (V5), using a method different from the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but double descent is a side finding. The paper's main conclusions are that GPT-style models store about 3.6 bits per parameter, that memorization plateaus at capacity and then gives way to generalization, and that membership inference follows a capacity/data-size scaling law. On double descent, the authors say it begins when the dataset's information exceeds model capacity. They give it an intuitive explanation: models are forced to share information across datapoints. They also note that the results may not generalize beyond their setup.
record.recipe_differences: The study estimates model capacity through compression-based unintended memorization and measures loss across training-set sizes; it does not reproduce the original study's model-size or epoch sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported transition depends on model parameter count; the authors say it occurs at approximately 10^5 samples depending on parameter count. The paper also reports separate synthetic-data and text-data settings.
record.problems: The relevant loss curves are reported only as figures, without numerical values in the text. The authors state that results are specific to their experimental environment and may not generalize to other datasets, architectures, or training setups.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant test-loss results were omitted. Other figure-only results on memorization, extraction, and membership inference do not measure the test-error behavior named by these claim versions.

untested.parts: No test-error sweep over model size. Only four model sizes appear, as separate curves.
Training-progress plots (Fig 5) show memorization, not test error over epochs.
Only GPT-style Transformers are used; no other model classes.
Only the sample-size axis is tested. Whether capacity predicts peaks along the model-size or epoch axes is not tested.
No label noise, no multiple peaks, no regularization tuning.
No reparameterized or effective-parameter recount of the curve.

missing.what: Train and test losses for models trained on uniform synthetic data (1.7e5–6.9e6 parameters) across training-set sizes. This is a no-generalization control relevant to whether a test-loss peak appears without learnable structure.

record.verdict_notes: All double-descent evidence is figure-only. The text's wording ('evaluation performance decreases as the training set size nears model capacity, and then rapidly drops') is ambiguous about the rise. The Figure 3 caption conflicts with its legend and the Section 4 text over synthetic vs text data. Rows r1–r4 and r5–r8 likely show the same runs on two x-axes and should not be counted as independent evidence. The capacity estimate comes from the study's own compression-based method.

versions.untested_parts: No test-error sweep over model size is reported to test the specified fall-peak-fall pattern.
Training-progress plots report memorization, not test error over epochs.
The study tests training-set-size variation in its GPT-style Transformer settings, not every model class or training setup.
The study does not test the generality of the curve across different model classes; its experiments use GPT-style Transformers.
The study relates the data-size peak to a model-capacity ratio, but does not test whether one measure predicts peak locations across model size, epochs, and sample size.
No test of label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization is reported.
The study does not test whether effective parameter counting turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.operation_detail: Varied synthetic training-set size and measured train and test loss against dataset-to-capacity ratio.
rows.note: The paper describes a double-descent pattern in evaluation performance as data size approaches and then exceeds model capacity; curve values are not transcribed in the text.
rows.check: Condition 'uniform synthetic sequences' is likely wrong. Figure 3's caption says synthetic bitstrings, but its legend sizes (1.7M–19.2M) match the text models of Figs 4/8/9. Section 4 (text) cites Figure 3 as the ratio replot. On uniform random data generalization is impossible, so test loss could not descend. Likely the same FineWeb runs as r5, replotted against the ratio. Values are figure-only. The state rests on the authors' wording.

source_check.notes: Figure 3's caption and Section 4 disagree about its dataset; FineWeb attribution is supported by the section but remains an editorial inference. Figures 3–4 should not be counted as independent replications, and neither supplies numerical loss contrasts.

statements.correction: FineWeb sample-wise double descent: Figures 3–4 and Section 4; model sizes: 1.7M, 3.6M, 8.0M, 19.2M; five random seeds specified in Section 3.2, whose experimental procedure Section 4 repeats; no numerical double-descent contrast or peak-location uncertainty supplied; Table 2 reports uncertainty for membership-inference results.
statements.problem: The FineWeb sample-wise double-descent report and model sizes are supported. The blanket absence-of-uncertainty description needs narrowing: the paper specifies repeated seeds and reports uncertainty for other results.
